newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk Nickel union plans strikes Mar 27, Apr 2.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk Nickel union plans strikes Mar 27, Apr 2.

text.p: Workers at Russian Norilsk Nickel's flagship metals plant plan to hold a one-hour warning strike on March 27 and a full strike on April 2, Valery Glazkov, head of the United Trade Union, said Tuesday.

"We will hold a warning strike of one hour on the 27th (of March) and a proper strike on April 2," he said from the Arctic town of Norilsk where the group's main mining and processing plant is situated.
Glazkov said that the extent to which the strike would disrupt operations was unclear, and that the strike committee still had to take decisions.
"We have decided that there will be a suspension of production, but whether it will be partial or whole will be decided later," he said.
He said the committee was considering halting loadings of residue with high precious metals content to the Krasnoyarsk non-ferrous refining plant, which is part of RAO Norilsky Nickel.
Glazkov said this was just one option under discussion and that further action may be considered by the strike committee, which met earlier on Tuesday.

"Of course we cannot just turn off the furnaces for one day," Glazkov said, adding that the 60 units of the main Norilsk plant, known as the mining and metallurgical complex, would decide for themselves how to disrupt output.
"Everybody should obey the will of the strike committee, since we represent the workers' interests," he said.
Boris Degtyaryov, the union's deputy head, had said on Monday that any strike would take place in mid-March, but Glazkov said the new dates were approved at the Tuesday meeting.
Glazkov said the strike committee had chosen six people to continue the conciliation process between labour and management.
The Norilsk Nickel group owes workers around 900 billion ($160 million) roubles in wages and holidays and another 1.2 trillion roubles ($211 million) to various budgets.
It has proposed clearing out wage and holiday arrears over the course of 1997, but the union is demanding speedier payments.
